evals.prompt: I ran `git rebase main` on feature/retry-429 and it stopped with CONFLICT in src/api/client.ts. Main moved the HTTP client into src/api/http.ts in the meantime. Fix it and keep going.
evals.expected_output: The agent identifies the rebase ours/theirs inversion, gets a three-way view, reads the history of both sides, ports the retry logic into the relocated client instead of resurrecting the old file, runs the covering checks, and continues the rebase.
expectations: States that during a rebase 'ours' is main and 'theirs' is the feature commit (or otherwise correctly names each side)
Reads commit history or messages for both sides (e.g. git log --merge or git log on the file)
Applies the retry change inside the relocated http.ts rather than keeping the deleted client code
Runs a typecheck or the relevant test before continuing
Runs `git rebase --continue` or tells the user it is the next step

evals.prompt: Merge conflict in package-lock.json and pnpm-lock.yaml after pulling develop, plus one in src/config.ts. Quickest way through please, I'm in a hurry.
evals.expected_output: Despite the time pressure the agent regenerates lockfiles with the package manager instead of hand-editing them, resolves config.ts by reading both intents, and checks for leftover markers.
expectations: Does not hand-edit lockfile conflict markers; regenerates the lockfile with the package manager
Resolves src/config.ts hunk by hunk after reading both sides rather than taking one side wholesale
Checks that no conflict markers remain (git diff --check or grep)
Summarises how each file was resolved

evals.prompt: There's a conflict in billing/discount.py. Our side caps discounts at 50%, their side changed the cap to 30% for enterprise plans only. I don't know which is right. Resolve it.
evals.expected_output: The agent reads the history for both changes; if the intents are incompatible and history doesn't settle it, it asks the user rather than inventing a new cap.
expectations: Reads commit messages or linked issues for both changes
Does not invent a new value or behaviour that appears on neither side
Either combines the intents coherently (50% default, 30% for enterprise) with justification from history, or asks the user to decide
Does not run `git merge --abort` without the user's agreement
